title: A junction of old trails
text: A bedrock mortar site near the original spring suggests that Native Americans regularly camped at what is now Freeman Junction. Explorer Joseph R. Walker passed this junction of Indian trails in 1834, and forty-niner parties split here after escaping Death Valley, some going west and some south. California registered the site as a historical landmark in 1961. By 1978 the town had died and its remains were removed by passersby, and today nothing remains.
